dossier.mechanism: EarnLock prices the doomscroll in body movement: every app you pick stays behind a custom Family Controls shield that shows the exact count left ('3,412 steps until unlock'), until Apple Health records your daily goal (steps free; active minutes or kcal in Premium). The goal is set on a calm day and the craving can't renegotiate it, and a 7-day Shadow Week watches before it blocks anything.
dossier.audienceScene: An adult on a phone at night, often on the sofa or in bed. They reached the page from a Google or AI answer for 'block apps until you walk' or 'Opal alternative'. They have already tried tap-through blockers and want to know in ten seconds what unlocking costs, whether there's a lifetime price, and whether their Apple Watch counts. Desktop visitors need the QR to get it onto the iPhone.
dossier.culturalHome: Digital-wellbeing and dopamine-detox culture (Opal, one sec, Brick), the 10,000-steps walking habit and Apple Watch ring culture, and the 'touch grass' / go-for-a-walk ethic. The developer frames it as a Sunday-calm self versus a Thursday-night self and 'a destination, not a wall' (journal: unlock-cost-outside-the-app).
dossier.mustProve: The first viewport must show that unlocking costs a number of real steps rather than a tap or a timer. It should show that number live and attached to the locked apps (the shield copy), that one goal unlocks everything until midnight, and that it is free with a $19.99 lifetime option. The working App Store badge must be there, plus the QR on desktop.
dossier.categoryDefault: The Opal-style screen-time landing page: a near-black or indigo-violet gradient, a glowing iPhone mockup in the centre, 'Take back your time', a stat row ('2h 14m saved'), testimonial wall, feature card grid. Its health-flavoured twin is a dark dashboard with neon activity rings, which the app's own green ring icon invites.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Pastel 'calm wellness': a sunrise gradient, rounded soft sans, airy whitespace, and stock photos of someone walking barefoot through a meadow (touch grass), with a gentle 'breathe' tone.
dossier.literalReading: Earn + Lock: padlocks, keys, vault doors, coins and piggy banks, as in 'earn your unlock' wage imagery. Only candidate 6 (lockout/tagout tag) uses the lock reading.

candidates.name: Trail junction fingerpost with walking times
candidates.why: Walkers read 'destination + how far on foot' signs by heart. The app's own goal picker already speaks this way ('≈ a 35-min walk'), and the developer calls the shield 'a destination, not a wall'. Carries it as follows: each locked app is a destination on a yellow blade with the steps remaining, the daily goal is the distance, and arriving means 'open until midnight'.

candidates.name: Shopfront roller shutter and opening-hours plaque
candidates.why: Everyone knows a shuttered shop and its hours sign, and the shield is literally a shutter pulled down over the app. Carries it as follows: the shutter stays down over Instagram until the goal is met, Premium partial windows are a shutter raised 60%, 'open until midnight' is closing time, and the reset at local midnight rolls it back down.

candidates.name: Transit day ticket and fare gate
candidates.why: Commuters pass fare gates daily, and a day ticket 'valid until 24:00' is exactly what hitting the goal buys. Carries it as follows: the fare is paid in steps, the gate opens all lines until midnight, Monthly / Yearly / Lifetime map onto travel passes, and Shadow Week is the week the operator only counts journeys.

candidates.name: Clip-on pedometer (manpo-kei) with reflective LCD
candidates.why: This is the original 10,000-steps meter, the walker's own instrument, read in daylight on a belt. Carries it as follows: the remaining count fills the display, MODE cycles steps / active minutes / kcal (the Free vs Premium units), RESET is local midnight, and the pedometer's 7-day memory is Shadow Week.

candidates.name: Japanese street vending machine
candidates.why: Buying from a machine is a universally known ritual, and on Japanese machines every item's price button lights once enough credit is inserted. Carries it as follows: the blocked apps sit behind glass with one price (your daily goal), you insert steps, and every button lights together at the goal. You are the operator who set the price on a calm day, and the machine's sales audit is Shadow Week's would-have-blocked count.

candidates.name: Lockout/tagout safety tag (the literal 'lock' reading)
candidates.why: Anyone who has worked near machinery knows the padlock tag that names who locked it and the only condition for removal. Carries it as follows: 'Locked by: you, on a calm Sunday · Removed when: 4,000 steps · No other key', and the once-a-day math-gated emergency is the supervised removal procedure.

candidates.name: Pedestrian countdown signal (hand / walking figure)
candidates.why: Every phone user has stood at the orange hand watching digits count down to WALK. Carries it as follows: the hand is the shield and the countdown is steps remaining. Ranked last because its cultural meaning is waiting, which is the wait-out-timer mechanism EarnLock argues against.

styles.label: Exact Steps Only
styles.lineage: Japanese street vending machines (jidō hanbaiki). Sources: the backlit display window with product dummies on shelves, the price button under every item that lights once enough credit is in, the dot-matrix/LED credit display and contactless reader pad on the control column, the operator's price-setting panel inside the door, the riveted maker's nameplate, and the sales-audit printout the operator pulls.
styles.thesis: The doomscroll is merchandise behind glass with a single price tag, your daily step goal, and the page is the machine that sells it. Every selection button lights at once when enough steps are in. This refuses the category's dark-gradient phone hero and its 'wall' framing in favour of the developer's 'price tag, not punishment'.

type.display: Dela Gothic One 400. A heavy Japanese gothic whose Latin is drawn to sit with kana, the voice of machine marquees and sticker lettering. Only H1/H2 on the marquee and plates.
type.text: M PLUS Rounded 1c 400/700/800. The rounded gothic of Japanese machine button labels and product cards: 800 for dummy names and prices, 700 for buttons and the price card, 400 for body at 17–18px.
type.utility: Doto 700. Dot-matrix LED face used only for real numbers: the credit display ('INSERT 2,026 STEPS'), live counts, dates on the nameplate.
type.rationale: Three faces, about 85 KB latin total. Dela carries the machine's shouting marquee voice, M PLUS Rounded is what a buyer actually reads on the buttons, and Doto appears only where a real machine shows a number.

styles.navigation: The machine's selection keypad. Six black rubber keys with white legends ('Prices', 'How it vends', 'Shadow week', 'Compare', 'Questions', 'Privacy'; M PLUS 700 14px) on a brushed-steel plate in the control column, as plain anchor links. The 'EarnLock' wordmark on the marquee links to top. On scroll and on mobile, a 52px sage enamel strip pins to the top with icon + name and a 'Keypad' key that drops the 2×3 key grid. styles.signatureInteraction: Insert steps. Three keys beside the credit display ('+500 steps', '+1,000 steps', 'Walk the rest'), or a range input skinned as the coin slot, subtract from the Doto display (INSERT 2,026 → 0). At zero, a class change lights every price lamp in one 120ms sweep, each shelf label flips 'LOCKED' to 'OPEN UNTIL 23:59', and the coil under 'Instagram' turns once. The operator presets (4,000 / 8,000 / 12,000) reprice every button at once. The whole demo is labelled 'Demo — illustrative, not your data'. No-JS: the window renders locked with the real price on every button and a printed line under the shelves: 'All lamps light together when today's goal is met — then every app stays open until midnight.' Reduced motion: lamps switch instantly, digits jump to the final value, the coil does not turn.
styles.motionGrammar: Mechanical on/off. Lamps snap on in 80ms, LED digits step in fixed increments, one coil revolution (600ms ease-in-out) happens only on a demo 'vend', and the pickup bar slides up in 200ms. Sections are static enamel: no scroll fades, no floating, no glow beyond a lit lamp.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and the 12 alternatives pages show the machine with its service door open. The corridor surround and a sage enamel marquee strip carry the page title (Dela Gothic One 40px). Inside, the backlit #F4F6EF window is the reading column: M PLUS Rounded 400 18px/1.6, 68ch, ink 16.6:1. Alternatives pages open with an 'Accepted payment' plate (EarnLock: steps | Opal: tap or timer) above the real two-column table. 'When should I pick X instead' is a printed notice, and the FAQ is <details> rows. Support is the 'Out of order? Call the operator' sticker with the email and response time. Privacy opens with the audit slip summarising the transparency row before the policy text.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. Enamel, coils, keypad, LED, plates and the pickup bin are CSS and inline SVG; product dummies are typographic (app names only). Uses the existing icon, 7 screenshots and assets/qr/earnlock.svg.
styles.risk: The machine can tip into a novelty prop, so the product window stays a hero-only device and every later section must read as plain set text on enamel or lit panels. A vending machine implies per-item prices; every button must carry the same single daily goal or the page misstates the mechanism. App names behind glass flirt with third-party trademarks, so names are text only, with no logos.
styles.memoryTest: A sage-green vending machine where Instagram and TikTok sat behind glass priced at 4,000 steps. When I 'inserted' steps, every button lit up at once.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

Dela Gothic One goes to shogiful-b, whose subject is Japanese. Set the marquee in Mochiy Pop One, a Japanese sticker/marquee gothic unused elsewhere. Make all price lamps lighting together the one move, and shrink the credit display to a small red 7-segment strip, as on real machines. That drops Doto here and leaves it on chessful-a and soon-c. Below the hero, keep the page on machine faces (side-panel plates, the audit printout, the pickup bin) instead of plain set panels.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

Keep Doto on chessful-a (a dot-matrix LCD that needs letters) and soon-c (a lamp grid). Set earnlock-a's credit display in DSEG14 Classic 700: a 14-segment alphanumeric LED face, 6 KB, with a comma and A to Z, so 'INSERT 2,026 STEPS' renders in one face and reads as a vending-machine display.

styles.label: The Junction Post
styles.lineage: Swiss hiking-trail signalisation (Schweizer Wanderwege): arrow-tipped yellow blades stacked on a galvanised post, each naming destinations with the walking time. Also the white location plate on top, yellow diamond waymarks along the route, the white-red-white tip for mountain paths, and the trailhead information board.
styles.thesis: The shield is a signpost, not a wall. Instagram is a destination 2,026 steps away, and the page is a waymarked route from the junction post (offer + action) to the summit (open until midnight). This refuses the category's lock-and-wall imagery and its phone-in-the-centre hero.
styles.scene: A walker at a trail junction on an overcast afternoon reads the post in flat, shadowless daylight, so the scheme is light (color-scheme: light).

type.display: Signika 600/700. A humanist sans drawn specifically for wayfinding and signage (low contrast, open apertures, legible at distance), standing in for the Frutiger-family lettering on Swiss trail blades. Used for blades, the location plate and headings.
type.text: Fira Sans 400/500/600. From the Meta lineage of Spiekermann's transit-signage work and built for long reading on screens; tabular figures (tnum) carry every step count and walking time.
type.rationale: Two humanist signage faces, about 120 KB latin. Signika sets the sign and Fira the guidebook, and numbers stay in Fira tabular figures so the step columns align like the time column on a real blade. No mono costume.

styles.readModeVariant: The location-plate header, then one yellow blade carrying the page title (Signika 700 40px) pointing right, then the white trailhead board as the reading column: Fira Sans 400 18px/1.65, 66ch, on the overcast ground with the route rail at left. styles.label: Belt-Clip Counter
styles.lineage: The clip-on pedometer: Yamasa's 1965 manpo-kei ('10,000-steps meter') and its 1990s LCD descendants. Elements: a moulded plastic shell, a reflective grey-green LCD with fixed icon segments (STEPS, KCAL, MIN), MODE and RESET buttons, silkscreened legends, a 7-day memory, and a belt clip and battery-cover label on the back.
styles.thesis: Your phone becomes the pedometer. The viewport is framed by its cobalt shell, the reflective LCD is the page ground, the remaining count is the headline object, and MODE cycles steps → minutes → kcal. This refuses the category's glowing dark dashboard and neon rings: a passive LCD lit by the sun.
styles.scene: A walker on a pavement at midday glances down at the counter clipped to their waistband in direct sun. The LCD is reflective with no backlight, so the scheme is light (color-scheme: light).

palette.role: Reflective LCD. The page ground and all reading surfaces. Ink on it 10:1
Active segment ink. All text and digits; also the inverse band (LCD-colour text on ink) for highlights such as the Yearly plan and the EarnLock compare column
Unlit ghost segments. The '88,888' underlay behind live digits; decorative only, never text
Moulded cobalt shell. Fixed viewport bezel, top strip, button panel, sticky bar, back-label sections
Silkscreen white. Legends and text printed on the shell (7.35:1 on cobalt), and the QR sticker label
MODE button rubber in the app icon's sage (ink legend 7.2:1). The one accent, used only on pressable keys

type.display: DSEG7 Classic 400/700. Real 7-segment LCD digit forms, used only for live counts, prices, dates and times; 400 sets the ghost '88,888' underlay and 700 the lit digits.
type.text: Hanken Grotesk 400/500/800. The plain neo-grotesk of silkscreen legends on moulded plastic. 800 sets the H1 and section heads on the LCD, 500 the shell legends, 400 the body at 18px.
type.rationale: DSEG7 is the only face that makes the count read as an instrument reading. It has no lowercase letters or '$', so every word, unit and currency sign is in Hanken, as on a real LCD's printed legend. About 60 KB latin.

materials: reflective LCD panel: flat grey-green with a faint 2% polarizer gradient, no glow
7-segment digits over unlit ghost segments
fixed LCD icon segments: 'STEPS', 'MIN', 'KCAL', a lock glyph, a 'PREMIUM' flag (inline SVG)
moulded cobalt ABS shell as a fixed viewport bezel with a 36px outer radius
silkscreen-white legends printed on the shell
sage rubber MODE key and a small recessed RESET key
white adhesive label for the QR
battery-cover back label (maker plate, no-transmitter privacy statement)
styles.firstViewportDesktop: The viewport is the device. A fixed 24px cobalt #2443B8 bezel with 36px outer radius frames the window; content scrolls inside. Top shell strip (64px): icon 32px + 'EarnLock' Hanken 800 20px silkscreen-white at left, nav legends at right. On the LCD ground, H1 'Block the doomscroll until you move.' Hanken 800 54px/1.02 ink, 2 lines, at x=72, y=112. The dominant move below it: '3,412' in DSEG7 Classic 700 at 232px over a ghost '88,888' (#B0B89D), spanning x=72–980, with fixed segments to its right: 'STEPS' / 'UNTIL UNLOCK' Hanken 700 24px and the lock glyph. The right LCD column (x=1040–1360) holds the memory rows: '3,412 steps · Free', '18 min exercise · Premium', '187 active kcal · Premium' (DSEG7 34px + Hanken 15px), with the sage MODE key (72px round) under them. The cobalt button panel starts at y≈740: price.value 'Free — Premium from $1.99/mo or $19.99 lifetime' Hanken 700 18px white, the official App Store badge 56px tall, and QR 120px on a white label 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. All visible above the fold.
styles.firstViewportMobile: Cobalt top strip 52px (icon 28px, 'EarnLock', 'Menu' shell key); fixed 6px cobalt side rims with 14px LCD padding inside. On the LCD: H1 Hanken 800 32px/1.05 (3 lines), then '3,412' DSEG7 700 at 104px over ghost '88,888', then 'STEPS UNTIL UNLOCK' Hanken 700 15px. Then the MODE key (sage, 56px) with the line '18 min · 187 kcal — Premium' 14px. Then the cobalt button panel: official badge 48px tall + price.value Hanken 700 15px white. Fold ≈ y=800. No QR.
styles.conversion: Smart App Banner sits above the shell strip (Safari). Apple's black badge sits unaltered on the cobalt button panel inside a 2px silkscreen-white keyline rectangle. The QR is on a white adhesive label, ≥1024px only. price.value is silkscreened on the shell, and plans become LCD price readouts. Sticky bar: once the button panel scrolls off, the bezel's bottom edge grows into a 64px cobalt strip ('EarnLock · Free — Premium from $1.99/mo or $19.99 lifetime' + badge 40px), full width on mobile. The closing CTA puts '0' on the LCD with 'OPEN UNTIL 23:59', then badge, QR and price.
visitorPath: Shell strip + LCD hero: H1, the giant remaining count, fixed unit segments, memory rows for the three goal units with Free/Premium flags, and hero.subheadline as the LCD caption
Cobalt button panel: MODE key, price.value, badge, QR, silkscreen trust legends ('NO ACCOUNT · NO SERVER · 0 THIRD-PARTY SDKs · iOS 17 + watchOS 10')
'READ ME' display page: the visible Quick Answer (quick_answer + speakable). The ai-canonical Quick reference <details> is the 'INFO' submenu below it (summary visible, content in HTML)

'7-day memory': the spotlight (Shadow Week) heading + lead, with seven LCD day cells D1–D7. Only the real example values are shown: Day 2 = 4 would-be blocks, week total 23, ~30m/day (screenshots 2, 5, labelled); the other cells show ghost '--'. spotlight.stats sit beneath
'How it counts': how_it_works as three LCD screens in sequence, 1 SET · 2 COUNT · 3 UNLOCK (HowTo), each with its full detail
'The shield': screenshot 1 large on the LCD with the shield copy, plus value_points (4) as a plain list
'Display frames': the 7 screenshots in a horizontal scroll-snap row, alt text as captions
'Modes & functions': features (9) as the device's function table (name | what it does)
'Prices': plans as readouts ($ in Hanken, digits in DSEG7: 0 / 1.99 per mo / 9.99 per yr / 19.99 once). Yearly is an inverse band; plans_footnote and Family Sharing follow
'Compared with': comparison_table on the LCD with the EarnLock column in inverse, the footnote and an inline badge; then alternatives_to linking to the 12 /alternatives/ pages
'Fits / doesn't fit': who_for and who_not_for as two columns
Back label (cobalt panel, silkscreen white): founder (Lagerland Apps · Finland) heading, bio, signals, support email + response time
'Questions': faq (14) as <details>

'No transmitter inside': privacy on the battery-cover label. data_collection none, notes, Apple label; transparency figures in DSEG7 ('0' SDKs, '0' tracking domains, network calls 'None'), linking to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
'Further reading': related_journal + the unlock-cost essay
Closing CTA: the LCD shows '0' / 'OPEN UNTIL 23:59' with badge, QR and price.value
Silkscreen maker line on the shell: Built by Lagerland Apps · v1.0 · first released 2026-05-22 · last updated 2026-05-22 (dates in DSEG7); other Lagerland apps; shared 'A Lagerland app' strip
styles.navigation: Silkscreened legends on the top shell strip ('PRICES', 'SHADOW WEEK', 'HOW IT COUNTS', 'QUESTIONS', 'PRIVACY'; Hanken 500 14px, +0.04em) as anchor links, underlined in silkscreen white on hover and focus. On mobile a 'Menu' shell key opens the list on an LCD panel. The fixed bezel keeps the strip visible. Focus ring: 3px #1C2117 on the LCD and 3px #F4F3EE on the shell.
styles.signatureInteraction: MODE. A real <button> on the shell cycles the big reading through the app's own shield copy: '3,412 STEPS UNTIL UNLOCK' (Free) → '18 MIN EXERCISE UNTIL UNLOCK' (Premium flag lit) → '187 KCAL UNTIL UNLOCK' (Premium). Segments switch the way an LCD does. A small RESET key shows '00:00 — resets at local midnight'. The memory rows keep all three readings visible at all times, so JS only changes which one is large. No-JS: the steps reading is large and the other two print in the memory rows, so nothing is missing. Reduced motion: an instant swap with no 80ms segment fade.
styles.motionGrammar: LCD physics. Segments turn on and off with an 80ms opacity change and no easing or travel; the count changes digit by digit. Nothing slides or reveals on scroll except the sticky shell strip (200ms). The bezel never moves.
styles.readModeVariant: The same fixed cobalt bezel and top strip. The LCD ground carries a calm column: Hanken 400 18px/1.6, 68ch, ink 10:1; page title Hanken 800 44px; dates and figures in DSEG7. Alternatives pages open with a two-reading LCD ('EarnLock: steps' | 'Opal: tap or timer') before the real table, with 'When should I pick X instead' as a plain list. Support is the back label with the email and response time. Privacy opens with the 'No transmitter inside' summary from the transparency row.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. Shell, LCD, segments and keys are CSS and inline SVG; DSEG7 provides digits and ghost segments. Uses the existing icon, screenshots and QR.
styles.risk: A fixed device bezel can read as a gimmick and costs width on phones, so it shrinks to 6px rims at 390. The low-chroma grey-green LCD ground can read as dull unless the cobalt shell and the giant count carry the energy. DSEG7 has no letters or '$', so faces must mix carefully in prices. Long reading on an LCD ground has to hold its 10:1 contrast with no texture behind text.
styles.memoryTest: The whole page was a blue pedometer. A huge grey-green LCD said 3,412 steps until unlock, and pressing MODE switched it to minutes and calories.

canon: Canon (the category played straight; not recommended): a near-black page with the app's sage ring glowing behind a centred iPhone mockup, the headline 'Earn your screen time.', App Store badge + QR, a 4-stat row (steps / minutes / kcal / $19.99 lifetime), a feature card grid, the compare table, then FAQ.
notes: The roll ran degraded (roll service offline, no catalog challengers, no quality-bar boards). Key d77c87e0, assigned 5, re-roll 1 = 4 (distinct on the first try). Neither roll hit candidate 1, so B is the honest pick. All seven faces were verified on Fontsource with the named weights (npm pack listing): Dela Gothic One 400; M PLUS Rounded 1c 100–900; Doto 100–900; Signika 300–700; Fira Sans 100–900; DSEG7 Classic 300/400/700; Hanken Grotesk 100–900. Data inconsistencies the build must not repeat or should fix first: (1) hero.cta_subline says 'pay once, no subscriptions', but Premium Monthly/Yearly subscriptions exist; reword before reuse. (2) how_it_works says the default goal is 7,500 steps, while the app's presets (screenshots 4, 7) are 4,000 / 8,000 / 12,000; the mocks use the screenshot values. (3) The founder bio says 'the studio's other 17 apps' and signals say '19 privacy-first apps'; both are hard-coded and disagree, so compute counts. (4) Copy says 39 locales but app_enrichment.yml lists 32 language codes. (5) The journal mentions CloudKit for the iPhone-to-Watch handoff while the page says WatchConnectivity with no server; reconcile the privacy wording. (6) alternatives_to includes 'Apple Screen Time (built-in)', which has no /alternatives/ page; render it unlinked. (7) 'Cheapest lifetime among screen-time blockers' is a superlative claim; keep it tied to the dated comparison footnote. No testimonials exist and ratings.count is 0, so no stars or quotes appear anywhere. Sibling watch: B's trail world may collide with Wanderwiki's name; A's sage enamel and C's sage MODE key both borrow the icon green, which is EarnLock's own and not a sibling's.

pageFixes.issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
